verses.text: The men of Kiriath Jearim came for the LORD's ark and brought it to Abinadab's house on the hill. They set apart his son Eleazar to look after it.
The ark stayed in Kiriath Jearim a long time, twenty years in all. The whole house of Israel mourned and longed for the LORD.

Samuel told all Israel, “If you're coming back to the LORD with your whole heart, get rid of the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth. Turn your hearts toward the LORD and serve him alone, and he'll rescue you from the Philistines.”
So the Israelites got rid of the Baals and the Ashtaroth and served only the LORD.
Samuel said, “Gather all Israel at Mizpah, and I'll pray to the LORD for you.”
They gathered at Mizpah, drew water, and poured it out before the LORD. They fasted that day and said, “We've sinned against the LORD.” Samuel judged the Israelites at Mizpah.
When the Philistine rulers heard that the Israelites had gathered at Mizpah, they went up against them. The Israelites heard they were coming and were afraid.
They told Samuel, “Keep crying out to the LORD our God for us. Ask him to rescue us from the Philistines.”
Samuel took a nursing lamb and offered it whole to the LORD as a burnt offering. He cried out to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered.
As Samuel was offering the sacrifice, the Philistines came near to fight. The LORD thundered against them so loudly that they were thrown into confusion and defeated before Israel.
The Israelites rushed out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, striking them down as far as the area below Beth Kar.
Samuel took a stone, set it up between Mizpah and Shen, and named it Ebenezer. He said, “The LORD has helped us this far.”
The Philistines were subdued and stopped crossing into Israel's territory. The LORD's hand was against them throughout Samuel's life.
Israel got back the towns the Philistines had taken, from Ekron to Gath, and recovered the surrounding territory. There was also peace between Israel and the Amorites.
Samuel judged Israel for the rest of his life.
Every year he traveled a circuit through Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, judging Israel at each place.
Then he returned home to Ramah, where he also judged Israel and built an altar to the LORD.
